interpretation: Core release is not every sentence of Aiyagari. Deferred/excluded entries remain visible and cannot be marked complete by a core build.

claims.claim: Natural debt floor and no-Ponzi
claims.disposition: Literal target with adaptedness and nonnegative, not zero, terminal limit made explicit.

claims.claim: Bellman, optimal policy, concavity and continuity
claims.disposition: General continuous assets, iid bounded labor, bounded utility. Lifetime verification is added explicitly.

claims.claim: Strict policy increase above a binding threshold
claims.disposition: Core contracts prove weak monotonicity and Lipschitz bounds only. Do not mark strict source prose covered.

claims.claim: Binding interval under its stated alternatives
claims.disposition: Finite marginal at zero or positive minimum effective income.

claims.claim: Inada and zero minimum imply never binding
claims.disposition: Unqualified note is challenged by an exact continuous-state counterexample. Atom-at-zero sufficient condition is separately proved.

claims.claim: Finite upper resource bound under impatience and eventual RRA bound
claims.disposition: Locally uniform strengthened bound; C2 analytic regularity explicitly declared. Does not imply finite-time absorption.

claims.claim: Unique stable invariant law and parameter continuity
claims.disposition: Mixing is derived from primitives. Stability means weak convergence.

claims.claim: Continuous stationary mean asset supply
claims.disposition: Resource law and asset/labor cross-section are linked; local common compact support supplies moment control.

claims.claim: No stationary distribution at or above the impatience return
claims.disposition: Reconstructed proof using value marginals, bounded Jensen and two independent finite shock histories.

claims.claim: Certain-income stationary assets and qualified precautionary excess assets
claims.disposition: At subcritical returns the deterministic stationary law is the borrowing-limit point mass. Compare the correct mean-income and risky borrowing limits; prove weak excess assets and strict excess sufficiently near the impatience boundary, without a global risk-order theorem.

claims.claim: Almost-sure asset divergence along individual paths at/above the threshold
claims.disposition: Not equivalent to absence of a stationary law. Supercritical and critical pathwise claims remain separately named targets.

claims.claim: Mean asset supply diverges as r approaches lambda below
claims.disposition: Clarida 1990 Proposition 2.4 supplies the target, not a proof. Proposed tightness argument closes it without an imported conclusion.

claims.claim: Natural-limit mean supply tends to minus infinity as r tends to zero above
claims.disposition: Use normalized effective income; do not assume raw effective debt remains bounded.

claims.claim: Stationary equilibrium for finite and natural borrowing limits
claims.disposition: Fixed-cap lower bracket derived, not assumed. No uniqueness conclusion.

claims.claim: Interest below time preference; capital and gross saving above certainty
claims.disposition: All equilibrium rates are allowed in the definition. Benchmark verification and gross-versus-net distinction explicit.

claims.claim: Asset supply can be nonmonotone; multiple equilibria can occur
claims.disposition: Permission for multiplicity is not a constructed witness. No arbitrary curves or calibrated-looking examples accepted.

claims.claim: Comparative statics of borrowing limits
claims.disposition: Only the two exact invariance/translation identities are contracted. Global monotonicity is not asserted.

claims.claim: Precautionary/risk-order comparative statics and Sibley/Miller links
claims.disposition: No aggregate risk ordering follows from a household-policy order alone. Needs exact risk/utility/cross-sectional contracts.

claims.claim: Government-debt neutrality under natural borrowing
claims.disposition: Exact pure-exchange/tax-adjusted natural-limit correspondence, not fixed-cap neutrality.

claims.claim: Monetary reinterpretation/existence of monetary equilibria
claims.disposition: Different return and clearing conditions need their own contract. Not covered by the capital-economy existence theorem.

claims.claim: Growth normalization and endogenous-growth extensions
claims.disposition: An Euler normalization identity does not extend bounded-utility stationarity to log/CRRA or endogenous growth.

claims.claim: Log/CRRA continuous-state model
claims.disposition: Not bounded above and below as required by this release. A separate weighted/unbounded-reward Bellman and stationarity track is needed.

claims.claim: Persistent Markov labor shocks used in quantitative analysis
claims.disposition: iid scalar-resource proof is not a proof for serially correlated income. No finite Markov numerical track.

claims.claim: Calibrations, tables, figures, grids and numerical algorithms
claims.disposition: Entirely outside scope; no numerical certification or solver development.
